commit.subject: fix(ledger): find a git commit inside Codex's shell wrapper

entries.text: Addition from the coordinator, fold it into your plan: Codex's workspace-write sandbox blocks writes to .git (git commit fails with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: Operation not permitted'). So in CI the common pattern is: codex exec edits files, then a later workflow step commits. That commit has no 'git commit' action in any session. Support it: a commit with no matching commit action gets the session(s) in that worktree whose last activity ended before the commit time and after the previous commit's time, matched as 'session' (a third match kind, shown in the viewer like the others), whole session segment since the previous commit. Keep sha/time matches preferred. Cover it with a test, and document it in docs/production.md (CI section). Also: the <path> commits are being re-recorded right now; wait until 'git -C <path> log --oneline' shows the wordfreq commits before step 7.
Let me verify the working tree is still intact after the lint-staged stash was restored by checking git status.
Commit 2: the commit-detection fix. I'm staging only that hunk of `ledger.ts` and `ledger.test.ts`, built from HEAD.

entries.title: git status --short · python3 - <<EOF · git diff --cached
entries.command:
cd . && git status --short | head -30 && python3 - <<'EOF'
import subprocess
def head(p): return subprocess.check_output(["git","show","HEAD:"+p]).decode()
def stage(p, content):
    sha=subprocess.run(["git","hash-object","-w","--stdin"],input=content.encode(),capture_output=True,check=True).stdout.decode().strip()
    subprocess.run(["git","update-index","--cacheinfo",f"100644,{sha},{p}"],check=True)
s=head("src/core/ledger.ts")
a='import { Entry, Labels, ThreadSource, type Action } from "./domain.ts";'
s=s.replace(a, a+'\nimport { unwrapShell } from "./shell.ts";')
old='''    if (e.type !== "action" || e.status === "failed" || !GIT_COMMIT.test(e.command ?? e.title))
      return;'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'''    // Codex wraps commands in `/bin/zsh -lc "…"`; the script inside is what runs.
    if (
      e.type !== "action" ||
      e.status === "failed" ||
      !GIT_COMMIT.test(unwrapShell(e.command ?? e.title))
    )
      return;''')
final=open("src/core/ledger.ts").read()
assert '''      !GIT_COMMIT.test(unwrapShell(e.command ?? e.title))
    )
      return;''' in final
stage("src/core/ledger.ts", s)
t=head("src/core/ledger.test.ts")
old='''        ["c2", ["1a2b3c4", "5d6e7f8"]],
      ],
    );
  });'''
assert old in t
ft=open("src/core/ledger.test.ts").read()
i=ft.index('    const wrapped = [')
j=ft.index('  });', i)
t=t.replace(old, old[:-6]+"\n"+ft[i:j]+"  });",1)
stage("src/core/ledger.test.ts", t)
EOF
git diff --cached

entries.text: lint-staged with partial staging should work fine since it stashes and restores unstaged changes around formatting — it handled the first full-file commit correctly, and partial staging just adds a backup/restore step that should behave the same way. I'll go ahead and commit.

entries.title: git commit -q -F - <<EOF 2>&1 · git log --oneline -1 · git diff --stat src/core/ledger.ts src/core/ledger.test.ts
entries.command:
cd . && export PATH=$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH && git -c user.email=<private> commit -q -F - <<'EOF' 2>&1 | grep -v "^\[" ; git log --oneline -1; git diff --stat src/core/ledger.ts src/core/ledger.test.ts
fix(ledger): find a git commit inside Codex's shell wrapper

Codex runs every command as `/bin/zsh -lc "…"`. A lone `git commit` there
starts after a quote, so it was never found and its commit fell back to a
looser match. Commit detection now looks at the unwrapped script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
